note: The island scenario (Phase 2). The cities, their sides in 405 BC and where they stand are history, carded in docs/research/island-405-395.md. Walls, men, grain, lean and every rule number are invention. Route lengths are invention too: straight-line distance between the sites, times 1.3 for the road, at 20 km a day.

nodes.name: Syracuse
nodes.detail: Your city. Its grain is your grain store, and its walls grow if you build the Epipolae wall.

facts.text: The peace of 405 left Syracuse to Dionysius.
facts.quote: the Syracusans shall be subject to Dionysius

facts.text: The marshy ground by the city bred plague in a besieging camp.

nodes.name: Leontini
nodes.detail: Free under the peace. Taking it breaks the treaty with Carthage.

facts.quote: the inhabitants of Leontini and Messenê and the Siceli shall all live under laws of their own making

facts.text: Stood a first siege because Dionysius had no engines.
facts.quote: Dionysius, having no engines of war, gave up the siege for the time being

nodes.name: Catana
nodes.detail: A Chalcidian city to the north. Its general was willing to sell it.

facts.text: Betrayed to Dionysius by its general, about 403.
facts.quote: Arcesilaüs, the general of the Catanians, had offered to betray the city to him

nodes.name: Messana
nodes.detail: Free under the peace. It holds the straits to Italy and a harbour for a great fleet.

facts.text: Himilcon wanted its harbour and the straits.
facts.quote: it had an excellent harbour, capable of accommodating all his ships

facts.text: Taken by Himilcon in 396; its people fled to the hill forts.
facts.quote: the great mass of the common people took to flight through the surrounding mountains

nodes.name: Gela
nodes.detail: Pays tribute to Carthage and may not rebuild its walls.

facts.text: Tributary and unwalled under the peace.
facts.quote: those of Gela and Camarina may dwell in their cities, which shall be unfortified, but shall pay tribute to the Carthaginians

facts.text: Sent its levy to Dionysius in 397.
facts.quote: He received first the levy from Camarina, then those of Gela and Acragas

nodes.name: Acragas
nodes.detail: Pays tribute to Carthage and may not rebuild its walls.

facts.quote: the inhabitants of Selinus, Acragas, and Himera

nodes.name: Motya
nodes.detail: Carthage's island town and its chief base in Sicily. Reached by a causeway and moles.

facts.quote: a Carthaginian colony, which they used as their chief base of operations

facts.text: Sacked in 397; the plunder was great.
facts.quote: the plunder yielded much silver and not a little gold

nodes.name: Panormus
nodes.detail: A Carthaginian harbour on the north coast, where Carthage's armies can land.

facts.text: Himilcon landed his army there in 396.
facts.quote: After Himilcon had put in at Panormus and disembarked his army

nodes.name: Aetna
nodes.detail: The fortress where the exiled horsemen hold out. Where exactly it stood is uncertain; the map places it roughly.

facts.text: The exiled horsemen held it after 405.

facts.quote: since it was an exceptionally strong fortress
